New and confirmed as Duffy's on-record statement: the outage began while L3Harris, which runs the network, was switching lines from copper to fiber at a remote FAA site, and a router involved in the work flooded the system; officials have not determined whether the router was faulty or the contractor erred, the site is unnamed, and L3Harris had not commented. Added more than 4,000 US cancellations Saturday as of 10:50 AM ET (FlightAware via Yahoo), the 2009 Harris Corp. router-misconfiguration precedent (Reported, citing a DOT IG review), and Duckworth's investigation call and Gov. Hochul's call for Duffy to resign (Reported). Not found in coverage yet: Bedford-specific remarks, center-by-center details, a redundancy explanation, new SMART statements, NTSB/IG review or hearing date, or how the $50 billion ask relates to the $30.1 billion request. Headline, at-a-glance and open items updated. [Yahoo News](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/live/faa-ground-stop-latest-updates-duffy-blames-contractor-l3harris-thousands-more-flights-canceled-saturday-no-sign-of-cyberattack-161329174.html) · [AInvest](https://www.ainvest.com/news/duffy-contractor-l3harris-working-telecommunication-maintenance-time-time-aviation-shutdown-2611/) · [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/video/6408377348112)

Confirmed (ABC, NBC, BBC): Mullin said there was "no cyberattack" and the public was never in danger, with no lives or flights at risk. Confirmed (BBC, NBC): Duffy said the airspace opened at 8:15 PM ET and recovery will take time. Labeled as unverified, because only one outlet has them: NBC’s Duffy quotes on radar and communications "instability," not losing all telecom or radar, and the 3,500/400 aircraft counts; BBC’s "few days" duration; and HuffPost’s account that Duffy blamed Congress for equipment funding. Coverage reviewed does not show questions or answers about the CBS reboot or Bloomberg FBI software-update reports, and does not quote the officials naming L3Harris, FTI, CISA or the FBI. The briefing open item stays open pending a transcript.

summary: The nationwide ground stop is officially cancelled: Advisory 005, event time 8:16 PM ET, signed 8:19 PM, for all airports and facilities, with no reason given and the next update at 11 PM ET. The 8:23 PM unverified-lift wording is replaced with confirmed. The stop ended nationwide at once, not by a published center-by-center release. After the cancel, ground-delay programs were cancelled at LGA, BOS, LAS, SAN and SFO (Advisories 006–010). Advisory 001 at 7:37 PM had allowed some coastal international departures, which officially corroborates earlier Hacker News reports of some Asia, Hawaii, Alaska and Europe flights leaving; specific HN flight numbers remain unverified. Aftermath: release times are being issued again; about 9,124 delays; O'Hare about 5 hours and Atlanta about 3; United, JetBlue and Air Canada are cancelling most remaining Friday flights; nearly 5,000 Friday cancellations. The Newark PENNS stop is still listed until midnight. No CISA, FBI or L3Harris statement; no congressional hearing or letter, though Sen. Cantwell said the committee will be reviewing. Corrected the Hawaii SpaceX item: Starship Flight 15, a precautionary West Coast halt, with no official confirmation of debris near Hawaii or that the halt was lifted. Added the expected Duffy/Mullin White House briefing (no readout yet) and a NOTAM-search note.
